text:
The text contrasts two perspectives on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme of inherent evil, suggesting that humans are naturally savage and descend into barbarism when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy posits that humans are naturally good and free, and it is society itself that corrupts this innate goodness. The similarity in presentation lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the role of civilization, but they differ sharply in their conclusions: Golding sees civilization as a fragile veneer over inherent evil, while Rousseau sees it as the source of corruption for an inherently good nature.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
